lesson.child_mission: Digital time shows hours and minutes with a colon (for example 09:05). Match digital displays to analog clock faces in 12-hour time.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write digital for: minute hand on 2, hour near 7. Draw analog for 4:50.

FEEDBACK
7:10; analog with minute on 10, hour near 5.

WATCH FOR
Writing 7:70 as a time is impossible — minutes only go 00–59.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Match ten digital↔analog pairs. Convert eight times both ways. Correct three invalid digital times and write why each fails.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Digital time shows hours and minutes with a colon (for example 09:05). Match digital displays to analog clock faces in 12-hour time.

Parent: Likely misconception: Writing 7:70 as a time is impossible — minutes only go 00–59. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

teach_steps.explain:
Digital time shows hours and minutes with a colon (for example 09:05). Match digital displays to analog clock faces in 12-hour time.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
